confusions: The skill says to write no comments in policy files and to keep statement as the guidance; fine, but the skill's 'Never' rules around fixing findings (ask first) sit awkwardly with a brief that says build all of the plan; I followed the brief and made the one function edit
Skill's fix guidance says a literal secret fix is a 'Do it' only when the user asked for a fix; the brief asked for changes to existing objects, so I treated the function edit as in scope
Nothing in the catalogue says what happens to a credential inside a URL built from $env parts; I could not tell whether url_credentials would still match, so the prediction is uncertain
xano policy parse printed the file back on success rather than a short OK, which made it unclear whether it validated or just echoed
wished_for: An example of an env-variable fix for a credential in a URL, and a recipe for Basic auth headers in api.request
A note on whether literal.credential_shape flags a literal that is only partly secret (one half a SID, half a token)
A way to run xano policy evaluate in dry-run mode for a new policy, so the prediction could be checked without a push
why_confidence: The policy parses and dry-run is clean, and literal.credential_shape is the right check for this ask. Medium because the check only sees recognised shapes and the policy is advisory, and it does not verify that $env is used or that variables are set. I have not run evaluate, so the finding set is a prediction.
